lines.text: betrifft das seinen Leuten entfremdete Lehen

unresolved.text: 'seinen Leuten': the possessor of 'seinen' (Wibald/Corvey or the Pfalzgraf) is ambiguous, so no beneficiary reference was set
'beruft ihn für den 1. November nach Köln': 'ihn' may be Wibald or the Pfalzgraf; the summons was not extracted

gaps.text: No act type for a command or order to restore; the order is recorded as rv:Enactment with qualifier 'befohlen', not as rv:Restitution, since performance is not stated
No role for the person commanded; the Pfalzgraf carries rv:Addressee
No way to express the prior alienation (entfremdet) of a fief except as part of a thing label.

corrections.text: Declared <urn:regesta:actor:22826:local:leute> a crm:E74_Group with label "seinen Leuten" and added it to <urn:regesta:22826:restitution-order> as rv:Beneficiary with nameInSource "seinen Leuten"; not identified with Wibald; producer of the restitution order set to correction-g10.

findings.subject: urn:regesta:22826:restitution-order
findings.description: The order is in favour of Wibald's side: the fief was alienated from "seinen Leuten", most plausibly Wibald's people, and the letter is addressed to Wibald. No beneficiary reference is given, so the factoid loses for whom restitution is ordered.
findings.proposal: Add a local group for "seinen Leuten" (or Wibald, urn:regesta:actor:RI004-002-W000420) with rv:Beneficiary; label it in source wording because the possessive is not fully determinate.

findings.subject: urn:regesta:22826:restitution-order
findings.description: The count palatine, who is ordered to restore, carries rv:Addressee. This matches the definition (to whom an order is directed) but loses that he is the party obliged to restore; rv:Obligor is a possible alternative.
findings.proposal: Keep rv:Addressee or switch to rv:Obligor by run convention.

findings.subject: urn:regesta:record:22826
findings.description: The summons of Wibald to Köln for 1 November is not extracted. As travel to an assembly it falls under the exclusion, but 22829 extracts a royal summons as rv:Communication, so the run is inconsistent.
findings.proposal: Decide one convention for summonses across the run.

findings.subject: urn:regesta:22826:entfremdetes-lehen
findings.description: The alienated fief is typed crm:E18_Physical_Thing; a Lehen is a tenure relation as much as a thing. Acceptable under the contract's thing and right split.

decisions.finding: The order names no party in whose favour the restitution is ordered.
decisions.reason: 'das seinen Leuten entfremdete Lehen zurückzustellen' names the people to whom the fief is to be restored, which is central to the order. The possessive 'seinen' is not determinate in the passage, so identifying them with Wibald or his people would be a reading; a regest-local group in the source wording is safe.

decisions.finding: The count palatine carries rv:Addressee; rv:Obligor is an alternative.
decisions.reason: 'er habe dem Pfalzgrafen ... befohlen' directs an order to him; rv:Addressee fits its definition and, unlike rv:Obligor, does not imply that an obligation is established beyond the order.

decisions.finding: The summons of Wibald to Köln for 1 November is not extracted.
decisions.reason: 'beruft ihn für den 1. November nach Köln' calls Wibald to a court gathering without a stated dispute; adjudications g5 and g6 treated such summonses to a court day as not required, and the run types a summons as rv:Dispute only where a legal proceeding against the summoned is stated.

commentary.t: Zu den Streitigkeiten Wibalds mit dem Pfalzgrafen von Sommerschenburg, zu deren Verlauf auch auf Ep. Wibaldi n
244) zu verweisen ist, vgl. Hausmann, Reichskanzlei 241 und Starke, Sommerschenburg, Jb. Gesch. Mittel- u. Ostdtl. 4 (1955) 37.
